question: How do you customize Django's admin interface?
title: Customizing Django Admin
direct_answer: Customize admin by creating ModelAdmin subclasses: list_display (columns), list_filter (sidebar filters), search_fields (search bar), ordering, and readonly_fields. Override get_queryset() to scope what admin users see. Use fieldsets for organized edit forms. list_select_related avoids N+1 queries in admin lists. Custom actions let you bulk-process selected objects. inlines display related objects on the parent's edit page.
interviewer_intent: Tests practical Django depth — Django admin is used in every Django project but few candidates know how to customize it effectively.

sections.title: Django admin customization
sections.content:
Django admin auto-generates CRUD views for registered models. The baseline is always @admin.register(Model). Adding list_display = ['field1', 'field2'] gives you columns in the list view. Adding list_filter = ['status', 'created_at'] gives you sidebar filters. search_fields = ['name', 'email'] adds a search box that generates ILIKE queries.

Custom methods in list_display: def full_name(self, obj): return f'{obj.first_name} {obj.last_name}' — add full_name to list_display. Set full_name.short_description = 'Name'.

Actions: custom bulk actions via actions = ['send_notifications']. Define def send_notifications(self, request, queryset): to process selected objects.

Inlines: StackedInline or TabularInline to display related objects inline on the parent's edit page. class OrderInline(TabularInline): model = Order. Add to parent ModelAdmin as inlines = [OrderInline].

Permissions: restrict admin users to their own objects by overriding get_queryset(). Override has_change_permission() for fine-grained control.

sections.title: Admin customization patterns
sections.content: from django.contrib import admin from django.utils.html import format_html from .models import User, Order class OrderInline(admin.TabularInline): model = Order extra = 0 # no empty rows readonly_fields = ['created_at'] fields = ['status', 'total', 'created_at'] @admin.register(User) class UserAdmin(admin.ModelAdmin): list_display = ['email', 'full_name', 'is_active', 'date_joined', 'order_count'] list_filter = ['is_active', 'is_staff', 'date_joined'] search_fields = ['email', 'first_name', 'last_name'] ordering = ['-date_joined'] readonly_fields = ['date_joined', 'last_login'] list_select_related = True # avoid N+1 in list view inlines = [OrderInline] fieldsets = ( ('Personal', {'fields': ('first_name', 'last_name', 'email')}), ('Permissions', {'fields': ('is_active', 'is_staff', 'groups'), 'classes': ('collapse',)}), ('Dates', {'fields': ('date_joined', 'last_login'), 'classes': ('collapse',)}), ) actions = ['deactivate_users'] def full_name(self, obj): return f'{obj.first_name} {obj.last_name}' full_name.short_description = 'Name' def order_count(self, obj): count = obj.orders.count() url = f'/admin/shop/order/?user__id={obj.pk}' return format_html('{} orders', url, count) order_count.short_description = 'Orders' def deactivate_users(self, request, queryset): count = queryset.update(is_active=False) self.message_user(request, f'{count} users deactivated.') deactivate_users.short_description = 'Deactivate selected users' def get_queryset(self, request): qs = super().get_queryset(request) # Scope: non-superusers only see non-superuser accounts if not request.user.is_superuser: qs = qs.filter(is_superuser=False) return qs

sections.title: Admin customization rules
items: list_display: columns. list_filter: sidebar. search_fields: search bar
list_select_related: prevents N+1 in admin list view
Custom list_display methods: return HTML with format_html for safety
Inlines: TabularInline (compact table) or StackedInline (vertical fields)
actions: bulk operations on queryset of selected objects

seo.metaTitle: Django Admin Customization — list_display, Actions, Inlines
seo.metaDescription: Customize Django admin: list_display columns, list_filter sidebar, search_fields, custom actions, TabularInline for related models, and N+1 prevention.

speakable_v2.hook: Django admin is powerful out of the box, but a few customizations make it genuinely useful for operations and customer support teams.

beats.content: list_display adds columns. list_filter adds a sidebar. search_fields adds a search box. These three alone transform the default admin into a usable data management tool.
Add list_select_related = True to avoid N+1 queries in the list view. Without it, displaying a related object's field triggers one query per row.
Custom actions let operations staff bulk-process records. Inlines show related objects on the parent's edit page — display orders on the user edit page without leaving the admin.

speakable_v2.cap: format_html() is required for custom HTML in list_display — it escapes the output safely. Never use string formatting with user data in admin display methods.
speakable_v2.followup_handoff: Follow up with Django admin custom views for dashboards, or fine-grained permission overrides with has_change_permission.
